articles.title: Brock Purdy Hailed as NFL's 'Best QB' by Fred Warner After 49ers Beat Myles Garrett, Rams
articles.summary: After throwing for three touchdowns in a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy received high praise from teammate Fred Warner.
articles.body:
After throwing for three touchdowns in a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy received high praise from teammate Fred Warner.

Appearing on SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt following the game (starts at 2:10 mark), Warner hailed Purdy as the "best quarterback in the entire league."

Purdy finished 25-of-34 for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. He also ran for 29 yards and picked up three first downs on the ground.

The peak of the game for Purdy and the 49ers came late in the third quarter when the defense stuffed Matthew Stafford's sneak attempt on fourth-and-goal from the one.

San Francisco took over and drove 99 yards, with Purdy accounting for 74 of them, capped off by a Deebo Samuel touchdown catch to extend the lead to 24-7.

If the 49ers are going to get this version of Purdy and their defense all season, the NFC West could feature the three best teams in the entire conference.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford, Drake Maye Make Woeful NFL History with Rough Stat from Rams, Patriots Losses
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford and Drake Maye, the top two finishers in the 2025 NFL MVP voting, made dubious history with their start to the new season.
articles.body:
Matthew Stafford and Drake Maye, the top two finishers in the 2025 NFL MVP voting, made dubious history with their start to the new season.

Per OptaSTATS, never before had the first-place and second-place finishers in MVP voting from the previous season seen their teams score 10 points or fewer in the season opener.

Maye and the New England Patriots lost 13-10 against the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday night in a Super Bowl 60 rematch. He had a disastrous fourth quarter with three interceptions, including one in the end zone with 26 seconds remaining when the Patriots were in position to potentially tie the game with a field goal.

Stafford, who won his first career MVP award in his 17th season, and the Los Angeles Rams were defeated 27-7 by the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. He wasn't as bad as Maye, throwing just one interception, but his 155 yards passing were his fewest since Week 11 last season against the Seahawks.

The 10 points for the Patriots were their fewest since Week 5 of the 2024 season. The Rams' seven points marked their lowest output in 75 games started by Stafford.

articles.title: Mike Evans Questions Rams' Australia Travel Plan After Learning They Arrived Day Before 49ers Game
articles.summary: Add Mike Evans to the list of people questioning the Los Angeles Rams' travel plans to Australia.
articles.body:
Add Mike Evans to the list of people questioning the Los Angeles Rams' travel plans to Australia.

Following the San Francisco 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday night, Evans seemed baffled when he was told L.A. only arrived in Melbourne about 25 hours before kickoff.

Evans wasn't the only member of the 49ers who expressed skepticism about the Rams' plan. Fred Warner said he felt like the Niners were getting stronger as the game went on, while the Rams "withered away" late.

The Rams compressed their entire travel schedule into a 72-hour window starting with leaving from Los Angeles for Melbourne on Tuesday night.

San Francisco left for Australia on Sept. 2 and arrived on the morning of Sept. 4, giving the team one week to acclimate to the time difference.

The game certainly played out with the Rams looking like a team that just got off a cross-continent flight. Their offense put up seven points and 290 yards.

San Francisco had 174 rushing yards against the Rams defense after averaging 106.8 yards per game on the ground during the 2025 season.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes gets Brittany Mahomes hyped with bold message ahead of Chiefs opener
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has found another way to build excitement before the Kansas City Chiefs begin their 2026 NFL campaign. With the Denver Broncos waiting.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has found another way to build excitement before the Kansas City Chiefs begin their 2026 NFL campaign. With the Denver Broncos waiting in Week 1, the quarterback has delivered a confident message through a new Adidas Football campaign. His wife, Brittany Mahomes, quickly added to the buzz with an energetic reaction of her own.Patrick Mahomes Sends Strong Message Before Chiefs OpenerThe Chiefs are preparing for a highly anticipated meeting with the Broncos on Monday, September 14, and Mahomes appears ready for the challenge. His name remains on Kansas City’s injury report, which had naturally raised questions about whether he would be able to handle his usual workload.Those concerns have since eased.Mahomes and head coach Andy Reid have indicated that the star quarterback is expected to play without limitations. That news gives Kansas City an important boost as the team prepares to open the season against a division rival.Mahomes has also been using the final days before kickoff to sharpen the sense of anticipation. His latest Adidas Football advertisement takes a dramatic approach, portraying patience and focus as key parts of finding the perfect moment to strike.The campaign uses a predator as a visual comparison for Mahomes, while his familiar No. 15 jersey makes the connection clear. The message ends with “see you Monday,” a simple line that feels especially fitting with the season opener just days away.For Chiefs supporters, the timing could hardly be better. After months without meaningful NFL action, Mahomes is once again at the center of the pregame conversation.Brittany Mahomes’ Reaction Adds To The NFL HypeBrittany Mahomes was quick to show just how excited she is about seeing her husband back in action.Mahomes shared the Adidas video on Instagram through a collaborative post with Adidas Football. Brittany later reposted the campaign on her Instagram Stories and made her feelings clear with an enthusiastic message:“LETSSSS F—— GOOOOO.”Her response captured the excitement building around the Chiefs' return to competitive football. It also gave fans a glimpse of the atmosphere surrounding Mahomes and his family as he prepares for another demanding NFL season.The quarterback has previously spoken about the support he received from Brittany and his family during his recovery and throughout the offseason. That backing could prove meaningful as he transitions from preparation into the intensity of the regular season.Now, the attention shifts from advertising campaigns and injury updates to the field.Mahomes will have the opportunity to turn the growing anticipation into action when Kansas City faces Denver. With the quarterback expected to play without restrictions, the Chiefs enter Week 1 with their biggest offensive weapon ready to lead the charge.For Brittany, the excitement is already here. For Mahomes and the Chiefs, the real test begins Monday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 5 Reasons the Cleveland Browns Should be Optimistic Entering the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns organization and the concept of "optimism" haven't always had the best relationship.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns organization and the concept of "optimism" haven't always had the best relationship.

Sure, there have been highs since the franchise came back in 1999, but there's have also been plenty of letdowns. The last few seasons of the Kevin Stefanski era were especially marked by disappointment and frustration.

But hope springs eternal, especially for one of the most fiercely loyal fanbases in the league. The Dawg Pound shows up every year regardless of how good the team is.

With that in mind, it's a good time to look at the team with a glass-half-full lens and break down the five reasons the club should be optimistic in 2026.

Todd Monken Could Bring a Successful Culture

Culture-building is essential for any successful NFL franchise. The teams that consistently win across the league have a lot of continuity and understand how to build a winning culture.

Todd Monken wasn't the hottest name on the coaching market when the Browns finished their job search this winter. However, his most recent coaching stops with the Baltimore Ravens and Georgia Bulldogs has placed him on two high-achieving teams.

He has his work cut out for him. The Browns are 8-26 over the last two seasons, but Monken has already established himself as a coach that's going to hold the line.

Monken had mutliple sound bites and stories from camp where he let the team know when he wasn't pleased with attention to detail and discipline.

That new energy and approach might be what the Browns need to turn things around.

The Rookie Wide Receivers Could Boost Passing Game

In a league full of dynamic receiver rooms, the Browns were led by Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond last season. Harold Fannin (107) and David Njoku (48) were among the top three on the team in targets.

The quarterback situation wasn't good, but their lack of weaponry certainly didn't help.

Hope has arrived in the form of two rookie receivers in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Not only are they both dynamic, but their differing skill sets give the Browns the potential for an interesting 1-2 punch in the room.

Concepcion was taken with the first pick and has already proven to be an all-around weapon with the ball in his hands during the preseason. Boston is the big-bodied receiver who has drawn comparisons to Drake London.

Regardless of how the quarterback play is this season, the potential of having two legitimate weapons on the outside is exciting.

Few things hurt the 2025 Cleveland Browns more than the offensive line. Whatever metric you would want to use to quantify offensive line play, the Browns probably ranked low.

Overall, the unit surrendered a league-high 29.7 percent pressure rate . In the run game, they were 31st in yards before contact at just 1.8 yards per carry.

General manager Andrew Berry didn't take a wait-and-see approach to improving the unit. They should be much improved on paper after some aggressive moves to get things right.

The optimism has to start with first-round pick Spencer Fano. The rookie from Utah looked good in the preseason and could be the cornerstone to build around for years to come.

The rest of the unit is made up of veterans with the kind of experience that is easier to trust. Tytus Howard is 30 with 93 career starts under his belt. Zion Johnson is a former first-round pick with four years of starting in Los Angeles and Elgton Jenkins has played just about every position up front over seven campaigns with the Packers.

The revamped offensive line might not be elite, but they do have a good chance of being closer to average than last year's iteration. Even average offensive line play could open new doors for the unit in 2026.

Andrew Berry's 2025 draft class might be the reason he's still the general manger in an offseason where the team could have cleared house.

There's no denying that last year's crop of rookies made Berry look smart in their first year.

Mason Graham's numbers weren't flashy, but he ended up starting all 17 games. Carson Schwesinger was a defensive leader from Day 1 as the team's second round pick.

Offensively, the Browns found a potential star tight end in Harold Fannin in the third round. He had over 750 yards and six touchdowns in his first campaign while the backfield duo of Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson paced the run game.

That's a lot of production from one draft class, but Year 2 will show just how high their ceiling is.

If they can build off the success of their rookie season they will give fans even more reason to be excited.

The Browns are a team that is definitely still trying to figure things out. The good news is that they'll see plenty of other teams who are also trying to figure things out.

Strength of schedule in the league can be hard to nail down from year to year, but the Browns' slate is going to help them regardless of how you look at it.

The Browns opponents for the 2026 season had a combined record of 124-165 in 2025. Only three teams—the Jacksonville Jaguars (13-4), the Houston Texans (12-5) and the Pittsburgh Steelers (10-7)—posted winning records last season.

Warren Sharp , who utilizes Vegas win totals to calculate strength of schedule for the upcoming season, ranked the Browns slate as the fourth-easiest in the league.

The early slate isn't necessarily easy. They open on the road against the Jaguars and follow it up with a road game against the Bucs, but this is a young team that should get better as the season goes on with games against other rebuilding teams sprinkled throughout the schedule.

articles.title: Rams' Puka Nacua acknowledges alcohol issues during 'darkest times' of his life
articles.summary: Nacua entered rehab in March. He could still be disciplined by the NFL during the season.
articles.body:
Puka Nacua told Netflix's Elle Duncan that "alcohol was definitely a thing" as he went through an offseason which he described as the "darkest times I've had in my life."

Prior to Thursday night's Los Angeles Rams-San Francisco 49ers game from Melbourne, Australia, Nacua explained what led him to check into a rehabilitation center in March .

"I was never one to share my fears, my worries," the Rams wide receiver said . "I was always finding different ways to escape from that tension, that stress. I think one, alcohol was definitely a thing for me. Just kind of drowning myself so that the issues and the stress that I was feeling never had the opportunity to be addressed."

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

The 25-year-old Nacua was a 2023 fifth-round draft pick by the Rams out of BYU. He immediately shot to stardom with a 1,400-yard rookie season. In 2025, he was a first-team All-Pro, the NFL's receptions leader and a second-time Pro Bowler after recording 129 catches for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns.

Turning into a household name overnight was something Nacua said he struggled to deal with. He was also co-parenting with his son's mother, which led him to isolate himself at times.

Nacua's off-the-field issues this past offseason also included a woman filing a lawsuit against him , accusing him of making an antisemitic statement and biting her shoulder. The woman cited gender violence, assault and battery, and negligence in her lawsuit. Nacua has denied the allegations against him. There were was also several other incidents last season, including appearing on a livestream before a game and agreeing to perform an antisemitic touchdown celebration.

The time in rehab, Nacua said, allowed him to have "open and honest conversations" and he's eager for the future.

"I'm looking forward most to becoming a person that I think my son will be proud of ... and as my son gets older, I can share some of the things that I've learned from the mistakes I've made," Nacua said.

Nacua has practiced with the Rams since training camp opened and caught five passes for 74 yards in the Rams' 27-7 opening game loss to the 49ers. The NFL could still hand out a suspension at some point this season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Cleveland mansion sparks controversy as neighbors push back over lake view concerns
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s return to his Cleveland roots has come with an unexpected complication. The Kansas City Chiefs star recently purchased a $5.35 million .
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s return to his Cleveland roots has come with an unexpected complication. The Kansas City Chiefs star recently purchased a $5.35 million waterfront estate in Bratenahl, hoping for privacy and a quiet connection to home. But plans for a fence around the property have reportedly sparked concerns among some neighbors, turning a dream purchase into an early test of community relations.Travis Kelce’s $5.35 Million Cleveland home draws attentionKelce’s new property sits in one of the most exclusive parts of the Cleveland area. The historic Tudor-style mansion, known as Moyenage, covers about 21,000 square feet across roughly 3.5 acres overlooking Lake Erie.The estate dates back to 1895 and comes with features that make it more like a private retreat than a typical home. It has eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a guest cottage, home theater, wine cellar, fitness center, sauna and heated pool.Kelce reportedly paid $5.35 million for the property after it had been listed for $6.99 million. Yet the size and location of the estate also create a challenge that many high-profile homeowners face: balancing privacy with the expectations of the surrounding community.According to a report from celebrity outlet Deuxmoi, the proposed fencing became a sticking point for some nearby residents. Their concern was that part of the original plan could obstruct views of Lake Erie from neighboring properties."A source tells Deuxmoi the couple is allegedly putting up a fence around the property and some neighbors aren’t exactly thrilled, claiming it could interfere with their lake views,” the outlet wrote.The issue reportedly prompted discussions with neighbors. Importantly, the portion of the proposal that would have pushed the fence farther toward the beach was later abandoned.“According to the source, that portion of the plan has since been scrapped,” Deuxmoi reported.That change could help prevent a relatively small property dispute from becoming a larger source of tension.Travis Kelce faces privacy challenge in BratenahlPrivacy is a major consideration for Kelce, given the attention that follows him well beyond the football field. Once news of the purchase became public, fans reportedly began showing interest in the property.That makes security especially important. At the same time, Bratenahl is a close-knit community where residents value their lakefront surroundings and relationships with neighbors.Local resident Sharon Klonowski suggested that the couple could eventually become part of a community fundraising tradition that allows visitors to see some of the village’s lakefront homes.“I don’t want to jinx it,” Klonowski said. “But I bet Taylor and Travis would do it in a heartbeat.”Bratenahl Mayor John Licastro also stressed that the village wants to welcome the high-profile newcomers while respecting their need for personal space.“We take pride in being a welcoming community, where people can feel connected to their neighbors and also comfortable enjoying their private lives,” Licastro said.“Part of being a good neighbor is offering a warm welcome, and also giving people the privacy and space to simply be at home, no matter who lives next door.”For Kelce, the move carries a personal meaning that goes beyond real estate. He grew up in nearby Cleveland Heights and has spoken about enjoying the chance to reconnect with his hometown.“Getting Tay back to Cleveland and showing her my roots is always something I love doing,” he said on the New Heights podcast.The fence dispute may be an early hurdle, but the response from local officials suggests there is still plenty of goodwill. For Kelce, the challenge now is simple: protect his privacy while becoming a good neighbor in the place he once called home.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL fans react to Netflix host Elle Duncan's gloves, NFL Big Js were wrong & Michael Irvin's insane hair
articles.summary: Welles Crowther was just 24 when he chose to save others in the South Tower on 9/11, telling survivors to stand up and help those around them.
articles.body: This morning, on the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we remember those we lost and of course we never forget what that day meant to this country. I want to start this morning with a story that most of us have watched over and over again – The Man in the Red Bandana. Welles Crowther was the same age on 9/11 as many of us reading Screencaps. He was 24. Born in 1977. Fresh out of college. He was working in the South Tower on that day when United 175 rammed into the building. Instead of saving himself and making his way down the one safe stairway, Crowther decided to save others. "Everyone who can stand, stand now. If you can help others, do so," survivor Judy Wein remembered Crowther saying. 9/11 HERO WELLES CROWTHER'S FIREHOUSE PRESIDENT REVEALS WHAT SHAPED THE 'MAN IN THE RED BANDANA' I like to think Screencaps readers have a little bit of Welles in them. We talk here quite often about taking pride in property, helping others and community. May we never forget Welles and the others who accepted the challenge on that day, and continue to take on challenges to make this country the best place to call home in the world. We're all beyond fortunate. 📩 Email: joe.kinsey@outkick.com Send photos, stories, tips, rants—whatever you've got. 📰 Screencaps Page: 👉 Read the latest Screencaps ▶️ YouTube: Screencaps with Joe Kinsey Subscribe for videos, rants, and behind-the-scenes. 🐦 Twitter/X: @JoeKinseyexp Tag me or drop a DM. 📸 Instagram: @OutKickScreencaps You guys need to start tagging me on content you're seeing. 📘 Facebook Page: Screencaps on Facebook 👥 Facebook Group: Join the Screencaps Community 📬 Mail (Thursday Night Mowing League): 27072 Carronade Dr, Unit A 155 Perrysburg, OH 43551 9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS Elle Duncan always tries so hard Netflix has a market cap of something like $320 BILLION, yet it acts like it has to be a startup. From Elle Duncan's OJ-like gloves to having Roger Goodell put on a kangaroo coat, the Netflix broadcasts feel so cheap. So contrived. So desperate. "She looks like she's ready to de-bone a Costco roast chicken," a Screencaps reader observed this morning. Couldn't have put it any better myself. Someone has to step in here and say no gloves. The gloves look dumb. They're a look-at-me ploy where Elle will now say people are picking on her over her gloves. Just watch. And then there's the kangaroo coat. Why? For money? Goodell himself was recently estimated to be worth nearly a BILLION himself. Just imagine what's coming when the NFL goes to Japan. Goodell sumo wrestling? Are tweakers bringing down Chipotle? – Tom in Clarksville, TN has thoughts on AI and the tweakers: Just a quick note to the best community on the internet. Always be wary of the tweet from the unknown kid from the company who is actively asking to be regulated by the government. The CEO of that company has now come out and added to the fear by saying they cannot predict the future, but all white-collar jobs are going to disappear in the next year or two. If this technology is going to kill us all, why can't it predict the future? Fear is an interesting emotion, this group of nerds straight out of central casting for a D&D movie are not Hollywood screen writers, but they understand fear is a great motivator. Anyone who has run a business knows you dont want the government to step in and run it. You especially dont want government to step in be the arbiters of superintelligence. More and more is coming out about this every day, the internet will suss this out, and we will discover what is really behind all of this. This is just my take, be wary of the guys with the very distinct hair styles. Start with the FTX guy, Karp, Aschenbrenner, Amodei, Altman... Also, since we dont know the future, I think Chipotle is on the way out with Wendy's...Lots of tweakers in there, I always get the same thing, and the price is never the same. Wonder what your readers think. Kinsey: I'm in Chipotle maybe once every 3-4 months. I don't really notice. There's a brand new Qdoba right down the road that is super clean and they give you like three scoops of protein. That's our go-to. Spread a little sunshine – CF in Kansas says: Loved Phil S. in Florida and his positive attitude. Like Phil, I make it a point to smile at people. I also try to find something about them to compliment. I once told a young man at the drive thru he had a great radio voice! It’s amazing what a difference it makes in their demeanor, especially if they have to deal with customers all day. It only takes a moment or two, costs nothing, and you may just make a person’s day! It also reminds you to always look for the best in people. #################### THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And with that, we get to work today. Let's go get at it. Numbers from : Stuff You Guys Sent In & Stuff I Like :

articles.title: Why is Andy Reid trusting Kahlil Benson with Patrick Mahomes’ blind side in Chiefs’ Week 1
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is expected to return from December knee surgery in Week 1. The Kansas City Chiefs may ask an undrafted rookie with zero college snaps.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is expected to return from December knee surgery in Week 1. The Kansas City Chiefs may ask an undrafted rookie with zero college snaps at left tackle to protect his blind side.Kahlil Benson is expected to start against the Denver Broncos with Josh Simmons sidelined by a back injury. Andy Reid knows exactly how unusual that sounds. His response this week was simple: Kansas City would not put Benson there if the coaching staff did not believe he could handle it.Why does Andy Reid believe Kahlil Benson is ready to protect Patrick Mahomes?Benson’s rise has moved much faster than anyone could have reasonably expected in April.The Chiefs did not draft him. They initially brought the former Indiana and Colorado offensive lineman to rookie minicamp as a tryout player before signing him to the 90-man roster.Now he could open the season protecting Mahomes’ blind side.According to The Athletic’s Jesse Newell, Reid has never started an undrafted rookie in Week 1 during his first 13 seasons with Kansas City. The Chiefs have not started an undrafted rookie in an opener since fullback Mike Cox in 2008.There is another wrinkle. Benson primarily played guard and right tackle in college. He took zero snaps at left tackle.Reid still sounded firm when asked about the decision Thursday.“He’s done a nice job for us,” Reid said. “He’s obviously shown us that he has the ability to play, and we wouldn’t put him in there if we didn’t think that.”Reid wants Benson playing with confidence rather than treating the assignment like a temporary emergency.“We’ve all been through that. I think when we first got hired, we thought we probably were pretty good at it. So, I want his confidence to be that and go out and play and just use his abilities and write a good story.”The Chiefs have another option in veteran Jaylon Moore, who has made 18 career starts at left tackle. Reid instead appears prepared to use Moore on the right side and give Benson the more demanding assignment.That decision says more than any preseason depth chart could.Benson started with Kansas City’s third-team offensive line during organized team activities. He worked his way to the second team and eventually earned first-team opportunities during the offseason.The Chiefs are now trusting that climb when the games count.How is Patrick Mahomes handling the risk of starting an undrafted rookie at left tackle?Mahomes is not treating Benson’s inexperience as an excuse.Heavy Sports’ Nick Roesch reported Thursday that Mahomes placed part of the responsibility for avoiding sacks on himself. The quarterback said his job includes understanding how his blockers operate and getting the ball out before pressure turns into negative plays.“You have to learn the guy,” Mahomes said. “You get reps with the guy, and you learn how he blocks and how he does things. And just as important, it’s my job to get the ball out of my hands. You can’t hold the ball and take sacks.”That matters even more against Denver.The Broncos have led the NFL in sacks in each of the past two seasons, according to the reporting supplied for this story. Benson’s first NFL start could therefore come against one of the league’s most productive pass rushes.Mahomes, however, said Thursday that he trusts the players Reid and Kansas City’s coaches put on the field.“So, I’ve got trust in anyone that the coaches put out there, because I know that they’ve worked their tail off to be at that spot,” Mahomes said. “There’ll be mistakes here and there, but at the end of the day, you’ve got to go out there and trust those guys and make the plays whenever the plays need to be made.”That leaves Kansas City with a fascinating Week 1 gamble.Benson went undrafted five months ago. He arrived at rookie minicamp needing to earn a roster spot. Now Reid is preparing to trust him with Mahomes’ blind side on “Monday Night Football.”If Benson holds up against Denver, his path from tryout player to starting left tackle will stop looking like a preseason story. It will become one of Reid’s boldest lineup decisions in years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “San Francisco 69ers”: Today host Allison Langdon’s unfortunate Freudian slip resurfaces amid Rams vs 49ers game in Melbourne, Australia
articles.summary: NFL News: History repeats itself? Four years ago, the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams faced off at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California – not Melb.
articles.body: History repeats itself? Four years ago, the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams faced off at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California – not Melbourne, Australia.But in 2026, the two NFC West contenders met again, this time on Australian soil. And that’s when a four-year-old television blooper involving Today host Allison Langdon unceremoniously resurfaced in the NFL conversation.Why? Because the Niners were back in Australia to face the Rams, making old on-air slip by the Australian Today host seem perfectly timed. Langdon had once mistakenly referred to the San Francisco 49ers as the “San Francisco 69ers!”Allison Langdon’s awkward NFL franchise name slip comes back online as Rams meet 49ers in AustraliaThe Australian Today host Allison Langdon became the center of focus in October 2022 after she accidentally referred to the San Francisco 49ers as the “69ers” while discussing an NFL game between the Rams and 49ers that happened at Levi’s Stadium at the time.The slip immediately left her co-host Karl Stefanovic and newsreader Alex Cullen flabbergasted before the studio erupted in loud laughter.Why? Because Savanna Young of the Daily Mail reports that “a sixty-nine is a sexual position in which two people perform oral s*x on each other, usually with the woman on top of the man, forming a shape similar to the number 69.”Allison Langdon, Karl Stefanovic and Alex Cullen joke about San Francisco “69ers”During a 2022 Today broadcast, Langdon was discussing what co-host Karl Stefanovic and newsreader Alex Cullen had supposedly been doing the previous day. Following that discussion, came her insanely viral line.“I assume we leave here in the morning and we all go home and parent our children. It would seem they did neither of those things yesterday.They were watching some footy game in America - the [Los Angeles] Rams vs. the San Francisco 69ers play… some rubbish game,” she said.Langdon quickly realized what she had said after Cullen instantly corrected her with “The 49ers!”Langdon laughed while Stefanovic and Cullen kept joking about the accidental X-rated wording.“That sounds much more interesting [than watching a football game],” said Stefanovic. Cullen added, “Yes! A lot of people might pay to see them.”Stefanovic said, “Yes, that’s what we were doing. That’s much harder to explain to your wife.”By then, Langdon could not stop laughing and had to bury her face in her hands in embarrassment!Rams vs 49ers Melbourne game revives old awkward clipThe timing of the resurfaced clip couldn’t be more fitting. The Rams and 49ers have now met in Melbourne for the NFL’s first-ever regular-season game in Australia.The much-anticipated matchup took place at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026, and San Francisco bravely defeated Los Angeles 27-7.According to Reuters, the historic game drew 100,000 fans as the NFL made its regular-season debut in Australia.The NFL had announced that the Melbourne matchup would feature the two NFC West rivals, making the connection to Langdon’s old broadcast mistake particularly entertaining for Australian NFL fans. And worldwide?Now that it has re-entered cyberspace! Particularly making its footing as strong as never before. Because? Cyberspace never forgets…sorry, Allison Langdon! You’re going to become a meme fest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 49ers easily defeat ‘withered’ Rams in battle of competing Australian jet lag strategies
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers easily dispatched the “withered” — and perhaps jet lagged — Los Angeles Rams, 27-7, scoring a decisive victory for hyper-punctual business travelers across the globe.
articles.body: MELBOURNE — The San Francisco 49ers easily dispatched the “withered” — and perhaps jet-lagged — Los Angeles Rams on Friday, 27-7, scoring a decisive victory for hyper-punctual business travelers across the globe. The NFL’s first game in Australia showcased competing, radically opposing strategies on how to battle jet lag in long-haul international travel with the Niners showing up early and the Rams late. “It was definitely worth it coming a little bit early,” said 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans, who caught 6 passes for 49 yards and a touchdown. “I felt like we got acclimated. DP (strength and conditioning coach Dustin Perry) and (coach) Kyle (Shanahan) did a great job of getting us there early and all the guys, we attacked it. We didn’t complain. We actually enjoyed being out here in Melbourne.” The victorious 49ers arrived in Melbourne on Sept. 4 for a NFC West battle that kicked off at 10:37 a.m. AEST on Friday — or 8:37 p.m. EDT/5:37 p.m. PDT on Thursday. “San Francisco was the smarter team because it takes at least a week to do this kind of big shift,” Dr. Mandana Mahmoudi, a sleep specialist from NYU Langone Health, told NBC News on Friday following the Niners win. “It was a very good experiment and the disparity in results showed.” The vanquished Rams, who entered Friday’s contest as a 3.5-point favorite, didn’t get into town until early Thursday morning Down Under time, about 28 hours ahead of kickoff. “It boggles my mind who came up with this strategy,” University of California San Francisco neurologist and sleep expert Dr. Kin Yuen said. “I mean, they have a lot of very smart people in sleep (research) in L.A., so I don’t know with whom they consulted.” Rams coach Sean McVay stood by the team’s approach despite the one-sided loss. “We thought that was the best plan of attack in terms of our approach,” McVay told reporters after the game. “We didn’t have the result that we wanted today.” San Francisco outscored L.A., 17-0, after halftime and 49ers linebacker Fred Warner said the Rams clearly weakened down the stretch. “I think it was definitely a matter of us feeling like we got stronger as the game went on,” Warner said. “The opposing team, it felt like they kind of withered away.” San Francisco appeared to have taken the more conventional game plan to beat jet lag, getting to its destination as far ahead of kickoff as possible and living a week in the new time zone to recover from a brutal 15-hour-plus plane ride. L.A.’s unconventional strategy was aimed at keeping the players’ body clocks on schedule, in hopes of tricking their heads, torsos, arms and legs into believing it was just another 5:37 p.m. kickoff. The fallacy in that approach, Drs. Mahmoudi and Yuen both said, is equating 15 or more hours in a pressurized tube at 30,000 feet to any other 15-hour-plus stretch of time on the ground. “They assume that’s as restful and it’s not restful at all,” Mahmoudi said. “You’re not getting the same restoration compared to the quiet of your own bedroom. You’re up in the air, the airplane moves, you go in and out (of sleep). It’s not like they each have their own private airplane, they’re all in that same cabin.” When the Rams landed early Thursday morning in Melbourne, the shock of seeing morning sunlight when it was early afternoon in L.A. must have been a traumatic bodily experience for players, Dr. Yuen said. “The brain is very discombobulated,” Yuen said. “The interaction with all of those environmental elements and trying to make sense of the whole deal, the brain gets very confused.” Still, McVay said he was not going to second-guess the team’s effort to stick with a normal domestic sleep/work schedule. “I don’t believe that’s why we didn’t play well enough. I really don’t,” McVay said. “Listen, I’m more than comfortable (with the travel schedule). That’s something I’ll always make the decisions that I think are the best for the football team.” The Rams ended up spending nearly as much time flying as on the ground in Australia. “It’s easy in hindsight to say it was a miss,” McVay said. “Those are responsibilities that I’ll take. Then you got to be able to look at it. I’ll always look at myself inside-out and figure out where I can improve.” At least a handful of 49ers had no idea they arrived had arrived in Australia so far head of the Rams. “When did they get out here?” 49ers WR Evans asked reporters after the game. When told L.A. showed up in Australia on Thursday, Evans appeared to be genuinely shocked. “Oh, dang!” he said. “I mean, you got to give your body time to adjust.” Janis Mackey Frayer reported from Melbourne and David K. Li from New York City.

articles.title: Patriots star AJ Brown has high ankle sprain as team suffers big blow after brutal Seahawks loss: reports
articles.summary: Patriots star A.J. Brown's reportedly sustained a high ankle sprain during the team's loss to the Seattle that could sideline him three to six weeks.
articles.body: The New England Patriots lost on Wednesday, but the hits kept coming on Thursday. An MRI confirmed that star wide receiver A.J. Brown sustained a high ankle sprain during the Patriots’ 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday and could miss three to six weeks, according to multiple reports. "I don’t know if he’ll be available going forward here for the next week, but we’ll see," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said. "Once we get the report, we’ll figure out what the treatment plan is." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The 29-year-old sustained the injury while trying to make a catch on an incomplete pass in the third quarter. Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett’s knee made contact with Brown’s ankle, pushing it into the ground. The three-time Pro Bowler was initially listed as questionable to return before eventually being ruled out. He had three catches for 26 yards while also drawing a defensive pass interference penalty that led to the Patriots’ lone touchdown before leaving the game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Patriots acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason for first- and fifth-round picks in the 2028 and 2027 NFL Drafts, respectively, with the hope that he could become Drake Maye’s No. 1 receiver and help elevate the offense. In Brown’s four seasons with the Eagles, he was durable, missing just six games and playing all 17 games in a season twice. In Brown’s absence, Maye will turn to Romeo Doubs, whom the Patriots signed to a four-year, $68 million contract this offseason, along with Mack Hollins, Demario Douglas and Kyle Williams. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Doubs had a crucial drop on second-and-14 in the fourth quarter that would have resulted in a first down. After the drop, Maye threw an interception on the drive, one of his three in the fourth quarter. The Patriots (0-1) will look to bounce back when they play the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road in Week 2. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Packers DC Warns of Kyler Murray's Game-Wrecking Abilities Ahead of Vikings Matchup in NFL Week 1
articles.summary: As Kyler Murray prepares to make his first start for the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon is well aware of the challenge that awaits him in trying to slow down the dynamic quarterback.
articles.body:
As Kyler Murray prepares to make his first start for the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon is well aware of the challenge that awaits him in trying to slow down the dynamic quarterback.

Speaking to reporters about the matchup, Gannon highlighted the ways Murray can "wreck the game" for an opposing defense because of his ability to make plays with his arm and legs:

"As I know firsthand what this guy can do with his legs and he can train wreck the game real fast if you're not coordinated the right way. We gotta contain him. We gotta be ready to plaster at all times 'cause he has just kind of a way of getting out that pocket and extending plays. And then when he's out that pocket is when I think he's most dangerous."

Gannon was Murray's head coach with the Arizona Cardinals from 2023 to 2025. Injuries limited Murray to just 30 games during that three-year period, but he was still effective with 6,612 passing yards, 989 rushing yards and accounted for 46 touchdowns.

After being released by the Cardinals in March, Murray landed a one-year deal with Minnesota, and it could be the perfect spot to resurrect his career.

The Vikings have a strong infrastructure with a good offensive play-calling head coach in Kevin O'Connell and a trio of wide receivers that includes Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings.

Adding to the issues for Gannon and the Packers is trying to slow Minnesota down without Micah Parsons as he continues to rehab a torn ACL. They allowed 110 points in the four games he missed last season, including the playoff loss to the Chicago Bears.

The 27.5 points allowed per game during that four-game stretch was up nearly 7.5 points from their average allowed in 14 games with Parsons on the field (20.1).

Green Bay and Minnesota split two head-to-head meetings last season, but the Vikings' win comes with an asterisk because it was in Week 18 when the Packers started Clayton Tune at quarterback since they had already clinched a playoff berth.

The Packers and Vikings will kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday from U.S. Bank Stadium.

articles.title: Can Kirk Cousins hold off Fernando Mendoza: Raiders explain why the 38-year-old is starting in Week 1
articles.summary: NFL News: Kirk Cousins won the Las Vegas Raiders’ quarterback competition. The harder part starts now.Head coach Klint Kubiak named the 38-year-old starter over.
articles.body: Kirk Cousins won the Las Vegas Raiders’ quarterback competition. The harder part starts now.Head coach Klint Kubiak named the 38-year-old starter over No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza for Sunday’s opener against the Miami Dolphins. According to The Athletic’s Sam Warren, Cousins earned the job through his command, experience and ability to operate Kubiak’s offense quickly. The question is how long those strengths can outweigh what Mendoza offers physically.Why did the Raiders choose Kirk Cousins over Fernando Mendoza for Week 1?Cousins did not treat winning the starting job as the finish line.“It’s less important to me than what you do after that first snap,” Cousins said, according to The Athletic. “I think it’s all about this entire season and winning the long game, and not just about the start of the season.”The Raiders already know Mendoza represents their future. For Week 1, however, they value what Cousins can provide immediately.Kubiak pointed to Cousins’ leadership and command of the offense as two areas where the veteran improved during his first months in Las Vegas. Cousins also has years of experience in variations of the Shanahan-style system.That familiarity matters because he previously worked with Kubiak in Minnesota, first when Kubiak coached quarterbacks and later when he called plays.Offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko outlined exactly what Las Vegas wants from Cousins.“Complete the football, get us into the right plays, get us out of bad plays, don’t make bad plays worse,” Janocko said. “I don’t think the blueprint has ever changed with the way we ask our quarterbacks to play.”The preseason numbers support that approach.Cousins averaged 2.32 seconds to throw, according to TruMedia. That ranked third among quarterbacks with at least 10 attempts and came well below last season’s 2.76-second league average.Mendoza averaged 2.95 seconds, which ranked 12th slowest among quarterbacks with at least 10 attempts.That difference could be important for an offense that allowed an NFL-high 64 sacks last season. Cousins’ quick decisions can reduce how long the offensive line has to protect him.His experience also showed before the snap. Against the Arizona Cardinals, Cousins recognized pressure on third-and-long and changed the protection. The adjustment gave him time to find Jack Bech for a first down.Tight end Michael Mayer expects more of the same.“He’s going to get us in the right checks,” Mayer said. “He’s going to get us in the right formations. That’s what I expect out of him. I think that’s what everybody expects out of him in this locker room.”What could push the Raiders from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza?Cousins can run the offense. The bigger question is whether he can stretch it.He averaged only 2.9 air yards per attempt during the preseason. Just one of his 17 passes traveled at least 10 yards downfield, according to The Athletic.Mendoza averaged 6.6 air yards per attempt and produced explosive plays with receivers Malik Benson and Jalen Nailor.That distinction makes or breaks the case, in Kubiak’s offense.While running Seattle’s offense in 2025, Kubiak oversaw a passing attack that recorded 57 completions of at least 20 yards. The Seahawks also tied for the NFL lead with 12 receptions of at least 40 yards. Sam Darnold averaged 7.8 air yards per attempt.Cousins once produced similar downfield numbers in Kubiak’s system. During Kubiak’s 2021 season as Minnesota’s offensive coordinator, Cousins averaged 7.7 air yards per attempt.The veteran is now 38 and several years removed from an Achilles tear. His recent interception numbers also matter. Cousins threw a career-high 16 interceptions with the Atlanta Falcons in 2024, tying for the NFL lead. He added five in eight starts last season.Las Vegas does not need Cousins to become a different quarterback. It needs his command and quick processing without allowing defenses to squeeze the field.Kubiak has already said Cousins is “starting for a reason.” Mendoza does not need to change that conversation in September. Cousins has to keep it from changing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Patriots Adding Defensive Reinforcements After Week 1 Loss to Seahawks
articles.summary: Coming out of a Week 1 loss and looking ahead to their Sept. 20 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the New England Patriots are beefing up their defensive front.
articles.body:
Coming out of a Week 1 loss and looking ahead to their Sept. 20 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the New England Patriots are beefing up their defensive front.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Patriots are expected to sign DaQuan Jones to a one-year, $3.5 million deal worth up to $6 million.

There weren't a lot of notable injuries on the defensive side of the ball for New England coming out of Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Cornerback Carlton Davis III briefly left before returning.

Christian Barmore missed their first practice of the week before returning on Monday. He went on to play 30 defensive snaps against Seattle.

Second-year lineman Joshua Farmer played just nine snaps in his first game back after a hamstring injury ended his rookie year in Week 16.

Jones is a 12-year veteran who has played for three different teams. He most recently suited up for the Buffalo Bills last season, recording eight quarterback hits and three sacks in 12 starts.

The 34-year-old Jones was originally a fourth-round draft pick by the Tennessee Titans in 2014. He spent seven seasons with the Titans before signing with the Carolina Panthers as a free agent in April 2021.

After one year in Carolina, Jones moved onto Buffalo where he spent the last four seasons. He has 34 tackles for loss and 20 sacks in 167 career games.

Since the Patriots opened the season on a Wednesday, they have four extra days before their Week 2 matchup with the Steelers. The reigning AFC champions are looking to avoid an 0-2 start for the first time since the 2023 season.

articles.title: Austin Barber doing more than just going home in Browns' season opener
articles.summary: The Browns' opener at the Jacksonville Jaguars was already going to be a homecoming for rookie Austin Barber. Now, it's going to have more meaning.
articles.body:
BEREA ― Austin Barber's quite familiar with EverBank Stadium. He's even familiar with playing in it.

The Browns rookie offensive lineman and Jacksonville native has been to Jaguars games at the stadium while growing up. While Barber was at the University of Florida , he played four times there in the Gators' annual rivalry game against the University of Georgia.

It's just that Barber, the Browns' third-round pick , has never played in a Jaguars ' game in that stadium. That is. until now.

Cleveland Browns vs Chicago Bears: Photos from 2026 preseason game

"Yeah, obviously you see when the schedule comes out and I'm going home for my first ever game in the NFL," Barber said this week ahead of the Browns ' Sept. 13 opener. "It's pretty surreal. A lot of family's going to be there, a lot of supporters are going to be there. I'm just excited to go back."

Barber's not just going home to Jacksonville when Cleveland kicks off the season against the Jaguars. He's going to have a major role in what the Browns do on offense.

The back injury that forced right guard Teven Jenkins to leave practice Sept. 9, and then missed the next day's practice continues to be an issue. Jenkins was not on the practice field Sept. 11, the final full practice the Browns will have ahead of going to Jacksonville.

The Browns will officially announce game statuses for the opener after practice. That's expected to be around 1:15 p.m.

That leaves Barber to start in Jenkins' place at right guard against the Jaguars. Which, again, would mean his NFL regular-season debut would be happening in his hometown.

"Yeah, that's a crazy thought, but I don't know," Barber said. "I just got to be ready when my number's called. It's crazy I'm going home for my first game."

With Barber expected to start, it would mean the Browns will have two rookies among their starting five linemen. Top draft pick Spencer Fano will be making his debut as well at left tackle.

The two rookies were two of the Browns' top five draft picks, all of whom were selected within the top 86 picks. There's a great chance at least four of the five ― Fano and Barber on the line, KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston at wide receiver ― start, while the fifth, safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, could as well depending on the personnel group on the first defensive snap.

While Fano was long expected to be the opening-day starter at left tackle, Barber's rapid ascension has been a bit of a surprise. The two rookies, though, have spent plenty of time talking amongst themselves about the entire transition from college to NFL.

"Me and Spencer came in at the same time and we spent a lot of time together, especially during rookie minicamp and camp and stuff," Barber said. "Yeah, just talk to him a lot. We bounce feedback off of each other and we talk to the vets as well. We lean on them a lot."

What's just as crazy as the 6-foot-7, 320-pound Barber getting to make his debut in his hometown is that he'll be playing right guard when he does go home. That's because, whether it was while he was at Trinity Christian High School or at Florida, he was a left tackle.

It's not even that far back into Barber's past that you have to look to find him in a different position. He was the Browns' No. 2 right tackle as recently as their preseason opener in Chicago .

However, a different injury to Jenkins led to Barber being shifted over to right guard ahead of the joint practice and preseason game against the Buffalo Bills in mid-August. Despite having only played three total snaps at guard, two of them run plays, it's been a revelation for the Browns.

"His development's been impressive," Browns offensive coordinator Travis Switzer, himself a former interior offensive lineman at the University of Akron, said this week. "It's hard enough for a rookie to come in and play, let alone when he's been at multiple spots. It's all about the approach and the way he goes about it. I mean he's wired the right way. He's a very diligent guy, he's very tough. So, we're excited about him and his development."

The development Barber has gone through matches an overall trait that's shared by almost all of the Browns' offensive linemen. Even when Jenkins was expected to start, they were going with five players ― Fano at left tackle, Zion Johnson at left guard, Elgton Jenkins at center, either Teven Jenkins or Barber at right guard and Tytus Howard at right tackle ― who have also moved around the offensive line during their college and/or NFL careers.

One benefit that Barber had working in his favor with the transition was the timing. It was almost instantaneous that head coach Todd Monken and offensive line coach George Warhop decided to flip him from left to right tackle, and even a move to guard was something they had even hinted at as early as draft night in April.

Howard, who'll be right beside Barber on the right side of the offensive line, understands that himself. He came into the league as a first-round offensive tackle, then played 64 snaps in his debut game in 2019 at left guard before the rest of the season playing left tackle.

"Yeah, I think that's the biggest key," Howard told the Beacon Journal this week. "I think Coach Warhop basically saw how smart he was and basically saw that and said, Hey, let's go ahead and get that positional flexibility, start working on him because we see him as a guy who can play multiple spots, and the earlier that he gets comfortable with it, the better. So if last-minute something happened, it won't be like a shock that he's been moved at because he's already done it before."

The transition to guard and the prospects of starting the season opener are all new experiences for Barber. What he's tried to do is to keep things normal in terms of a routine.

That process, Barber admits, has changed since he arrived with the Browns just because of the time commitment compared to while he was in college. The extra time has mostly been spent watching more of the Jaguars' talented defensive front, which includes former No. 1 overall pick Travon Walker and two-time Pro Bowler Josh Hines-Allen at the ends and 12-year vet Arik Armstead and former Ohio State Buckeye DaVon Hamilton inside.

"They're a really good front," Barber said. " Josh Allen 's been there forever and Armstead's been in the league for a long time. They're vets. They're really good. You got to be ready for what they do and you got to be ready to go."

articles.title: NFLPA names Laremy Tunsil their Community MVP for Week 1
articles.summary: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Commanders offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil has been named their Community MVP for Week 1 of the 2026 seas...
articles.body:
The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Commanders offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil has been named their Community MVP for Week 1 of the 2026 season.

Tunsil is being honored for hosting a back-to-school event for 250 kids in the Washington D.C. area. The children and their families enjoyed food and music while receiving a backpack with school supplies, haircuts and other items to help get ready for the start of the school year.

"Being named this week's NFLPA Community MVP means a lot to me because giving back has always been bigger than football," Tunsil said in a statement. "I'm grateful to have the opportunity to support families, empower young people and create experiences that make a difference in my community."

The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to an organization of Tunsil's choice. Tunsil, who is currently sidelined by a triceps injury, will also be eligible for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.

articles.title: The 49ers make their case as a contender with season-opening 27-7 win over the Rams
articles.summary: In the nearly seven months since the San Francisco 49ers last played a game that counted, they watched the Seattle Seahawks celebrate a Super Bowl win in the...
articles.body:
In the nearly seven months since the San Francisco 49ers last played a game that counted, they watched the Seattle Seahawks celebrate a Super Bowl win in the Niners' home locker room and the Los Angeles Rams get all the hype after an offseason that featured the addition of Myles Garrett .

While San Francisco 's NFC West rivals may have gotten lots of the hype, the Niners showed that they might also belong on the short list of Super Bowl contenders after beating the Rams 27-7 in the season opener in Australia.

Much of the attention leading up to the game was focused on the Rams' decision to arrive in Australia on Thursday, about 24 hours before kickoff, but the 49ers enjoyed their weeklong stay Down Under and came out with the win.

"We were just focused on us," linebacker Dre Greenlaw said. "We knew what we had to do. We know the standard that we play with. If they wanted to come in the day before, the week before, it didn't matter at all. We got a standard that we play with, so for us it wasn't even about how they were going to come out, it was about how we were going to come out."

The defense shut down QB Matthew Stafford and an offense that led the NFL in scoring last season. The offense neutralized Garrett and got three touchdown passes from an efficient Brock Purdy . The special teams even contributed with Deebo Samuel 's 45-yard kickoff return that set up a touchdown to start the second half.

San Francisco then broke open a three-point game and won easily.

"I think it was definitely a matter of us feeling like we got stronger as the game went on versus the opposing team. It felt like they kind of withered away," linebacker Fred Warner said. "Our plan was great coming out here early and all the resources they gave us to be successful for today is what gave us a chance to win this game."

Purdy to Mike Evans connection. It didn't take long at all for Evans to make an impact on the Niners after leaving Tampa Bay to sign as a free agent in the offseason. He had three third-down conversion catches on the opening field goal drive, marking the first team a 49ers player had done that in five years. He finished with six catches for 49 yards and a touchdown. Five of those catches came on third down conversions, including a 2-yard TD on a fade pass in the third quarter.

Sacking the quarterback. The 49ers ranked last in the NFL with 20 sacks last year and got none in Week 1. Nick Bosa had a key pressure on the first drive in his first game back from a torn ACL and played very well against the run. Offseason acquisition Osa Odighizuwa had a team-high five pressures and provided a strong interior rush.

Raheem Morris. The team's new defensive coordinator had an impressive debut by holding the Rams to their fewest points in 85 regular season or playoff games started by Stafford. The defensive backs have raved about his approach, which allows them to be more aggressive and helped lead to a first half interception by Renardo Green . The biggest play came when the Niners stuffed Stafford on a fourth-down sneak from the 1 in the third quarter.

Young receivers. The 49ers have been trying to get younger at receiver through the draft but it hasn't led to production. Ricky Pearsall , a first-round pick in 2024, is out for the season with a knee injury. Jordan Watkins , a fourth-round pick in 2025, was a healthy scratch for Week 1. Rookie De'Zhaunn Stribling was being counted on heavily after a strong preseason but injured his ankle early and had no catches in his debut.

Shanahan said Stribling's Achilles' was intact but he will need more tests to determine the extent of the injury to the ankle. ... TE Jake Tonges left the game with an MCL injury and will miss some time.

36. Christian McCaffrey 's 36 snaps were his fewest in a game he didn't leave with an injury since his first season in San Francisco in 2022. The Niners had talked about lightening his workload after he led the NFL with 413 touches from scrimmage in the 2025 regular season. Rookie Kaelon Black helped make that possible by rushing 14 times for 65 yards.

The 49ers host Miami on Sept. 20 in search of their fifth 2-0 start in 10 seasons under Shanahan. They made the playoffs the previous four with two trips to the Super Bowl.
